svg.text: AzureAgentForge — Self-Hosted Primary · Cloud Warm Standby
Owned hardware runs the stack · Azure sleeps until a lease flip · steady-state ≈ $35–45/mo · reference topology
Public edge · one Cloudflare tunnel — the hostname never moves
Operator control plane · every failover is a deliberate action
flips lease · syncs shares · wakes / sleeps cloud
Self-hosted primary site · owned hardware (Apple-silicon mini / mini-PC / WSL2) · normally holds the lease
Docker Compose stack · deploy/mac-site (shared with windows-site) · brought up only via the site switch
refuses to start the stack unless the
this site holds the lease · same tunnel as standby
connects out to the shared Flexible Server
written by the site switch before every bring-up —
the host never holds a service principal
Host automation · launchd (macOS) / Task Scheduler → WSL2 (Windows) · each job is a no-op without the lease
boot-guard · startup + every 5 min — stops the stack if the authoritative lease moved (does nothing on Key Vault errors)
image freshness · every 10 min — registry login + compose pull; roll the live profile only on a digest change
firewall keeper · every 15 min — upsert the shared-PG "home-ip" rule when the home WAN address rotates
warm-standby share sync · hourly — azcopy the file shares local→cloud; stamps standby_sync_completed for the watchdog
skill curator · daily — one-shot maintenance job (compose "jobs" profile)
Azure region · warm standby compute + the shared data plane
Container Apps Environment — DORMANT · scale-to-zero / asleep · woken only by aaf-site cloud
same images · same tunnel · same shared DB — a lease flip makes this the live site
with shares at most one hour stale
always-on · the failover pivot — the database never moves
both sites connect over the public endpoint, IP-firewalled,
sslmode=require · pgvector · RPO ≈ 0 for a site switch
plus app credentials · public access default-deny + IP allowlist
one image source for both sites
standby copy, refreshed by the hourly
steady-state cloud spend ≈ $35–45/mo — the always-on shared server is the price of RPO-0 failover
egress from whichever site is live,
always via the Model Router (budget caps)
TLS · public endpoint · IP-firewalled — crosses both site boundaries; the DB itself never moves
azcopy · hourly · shares only — never the database
second connector · same tunnel · idle until the lease flips
dashed = site / trust boundary (slate = owned hardware, blue = Azure)
dotted = lease / control / secret access · green dashed = hourly share sync
